explanation: Traverse the BST in reverse inorder: right subtree, node, left subtree. This visits keys in nonincreasing order, so stop as soon as k values have been collected.
timeComplexity: O(h + k) time for height h.
spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space, plus O(k) output space.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Reverse inorder visits every right-subtree key before its root and then its left-subtree keys, so BST values appear in nonincreasing order. Stopping after k visits therefore returns exactly the k largest keys.
walkthrough: For [7,3,11,1,5,9,13], reverse inorder begins 13,11,9,7. With k=3, stop after [13,11,9].
edgeCases: Stop before traversing unnecessary smaller subtrees.
k=0 returns an empty result when supplied.
Preserve repeated keys if the EPI BST input permits them.
